knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $2a+b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+b &= 2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -7\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -7\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}2+(-14) \\ -4+(-7)\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|2a+b| &= \sqrt{(-12)^2+(-11)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{265} \\
&= \sqrt{265}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $2a+b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{265}}\cdot (2a+b) \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{265}}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}- \frac{12 \sqrt{265}}{265} \\ - \frac{11 \sqrt{265}}{265}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $a+2b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2b &= \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ -12\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}1+(-12) \\ 0+(-12)\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+2b| &= \sqrt{(-11)^2+(-12)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{265} \\
&= \sqrt{265}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $a+2b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{265}}\cdot (a+2b) \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{265}}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -12\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}- \frac{11 \sqrt{265}}{265} \\ - \frac{12 \sqrt{265}}{265}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
